# Shivani

> Portfolio of Shivani, an AI/ML Engineer working on generative AI, LLMs, RAG, agentic AI, multi-agent systems, orchestrators, NLP, Python, LangGraph, UI, backend, front-end and full stack development.

The site describes the services on offer and publishes general technical guides. Wayfarer is a live project. The home page also lists other systems Shivani can build.

## Main pages

- [Home](/): overview, skills, projects and contact form
- [Services](/services/): all services
- [Blog](/blog/): all technical guides

## Services

- [Generative AI and LLM development](/services/generative-ai-llm-development/): software features built on large language models
- [RAG development](/services/rag-development/): systems that ground LLM answers in your own content
- [Multi-agent systems development](/services/multi-agent-systems/): specialised agents with clear roles, controlled tools and visible limits
- [AI orchestration with LangGraph](/services/ai-orchestration-langgraph/): the control layer for routing, state, recovery and pauses
- [NLP development in Python](/services/nlp-development/): classifying, extracting, searching and summarising text
- [Full stack development for AI products](/services/full-stack-development/): the backend, front-end and UI around a model or agent

## Guides

- [What RAG is and when to use it](/blog/what-is-rag-and-when-to-use-it/): how RAG works and when it is the wrong tool
- [Choosing chunking strategies for RAG](/blog/choosing-chunking-strategies-for-rag/): comparing ways to split documents
- [How to evaluate a RAG system](/blog/how-to-evaluate-a-rag-system/): measuring retrieval and answer quality
- [Hybrid search and reranking for RAG](/blog/hybrid-search-and-reranking-for-rag/): combining keyword and vector search and reordering results
- [Single agent vs multi-agent systems](/blog/single-agent-vs-multi-agent-systems/): comparing the two designs and choosing between them
- [Building an orchestrator with LangGraph](/blog/building-an-orchestrator-with-langgraph/): state, nodes, routing, checkpointing and review
- [Human-in-the-loop approval for AI agents](/blog/human-in-the-loop-approval-for-ai-agents/): what to gate, resuming safely and avoiding approval fatigue
- [Adding an LLM feature to a full stack app](/blog/adding-an-llm-feature-to-a-full-stack-app/): backend, front-end and operational decisions
- [Streaming LLM responses to a web UI](/blog/streaming-llm-responses-to-a-web-ui/): transports, events, rendering, cancellation and proxies
- [LLM guardrails and prompt injection defence](/blog/llm-guardrails-and-prompt-injection-defence/): layered defences that limit damage from a manipulated model
- [Text classification with LLMs vs traditional NLP](/blog/text-classification-llms-vs-traditional-nlp/): comparing methods, testing them fairly and combining them in a cascade
- [Named entity recognition and data extraction with LLMs](/blog/named-entity-recognition-and-data-extraction-with-llms/): schemas, validation, grounding checks and field-level measurement
- [Agent memory: short-term and long-term state](/blog/agent-memory-short-term-and-long-term-state/): managing run state and designing, retrieving and securing long-term memory
- [Tool calling for AI agents: designing reliable tools](/blog/tool-calling-for-ai-agents/): schemas, validation, actionable errors, idempotency, loop limits and testing
- [Building a backend API for an AI agent in Python](/blog/building-a-backend-api-for-an-ai-agent-in-python/): framework-neutral design of runs, workers, idempotency, cancellation and testing
- [LangChain vs LangGraph: when to use each](/blog/langchain-vs-langgraph-when-to-use-each/): choosing by control flow, using both together and knowing when plain code is enough
- [Serving an LLM app with FastAPI: structure and async](/blog/serving-an-llm-app-with-fastapi/): project layout, shared clients, the event loop, concurrency limits, disconnects and test overrides
- [Embeddings and choosing a vector database](/blog/embeddings-and-choosing-a-vector-database/): how embeddings work and the criteria for selecting a model and a vector store, with no product rankings
- [Text-to-SQL agents: risks and safeguards](/blog/text-to-sql-agents-risks-and-safeguards/): data exposure, wrong answers, database permissions, query validation, resource limits and testing
- [Controlling LLM cost and latency](/blog/controlling-llm-cost-and-latency/): measurement, context trimming, model routing, caching, output caps, streaming and agent loop limits
- [RAG vs fine-tuning: which to choose](/blog/rag-vs-fine-tuning/): diagnosing knowledge problems and behaviour problems, comparing the trade-offs and combining the two
- [Agentic RAG explained: when it beats a plain pipeline](/blog/agentic-rag-explained/): how a model can control retrieval, the common patterns and when a fixed pipeline remains the better choice
- [Model Context Protocol: what it is and how agents use it](/blog/model-context-protocol-for-ai-agents/): hosts, clients and servers, how agents discover and call tools, transports and the security decisions that remain yours
- [CrewAI vs LangGraph for multi-agent systems](/blog/crewai-vs-langgraph/): comparing role-based crews with explicit graphs on control, state, recovery and human review, and how to test the choice
- [How to build a RAG chatbot in Python](/blog/build-a-rag-chatbot-in-python/): a provider-neutral walkthrough of chunking, indexing, retrieval, cited answers, follow-up questions and testing
- [What agentic AI is, and how it differs from chatbots and automation](/blog/what-is-agentic-ai/): What makes a system agentic, how it differs from chatbots and rule-based automation, and how to judge whether a task justifies the extra risk and cost.
- [How to build an AI agent in Python, step by step](/blog/how-to-build-an-ai-agent-in-python/): A step-by-step Python walkthrough: scoping the job, defining validated tools, writing the agent loop, setting hard limits, logging each step and testing with a scripted model.
- [Structured output from LLMs: getting reliable JSON](/blog/structured-output-from-llms/): How to get dependable JSON from a language model: choosing a schema-constrained mode, validating in code, handling refusals and truncation, and catching valid but wrong data.
- [LLM observability and tracing: monitoring LLM apps in production](/blog/llm-observability-and-tracing/): How to see what an LLM app is doing in production: what to trace, which metrics to alert on, OpenTelemetry GenAI conventions, handling sensitive prompts and scoring live quality.
- [pgvector vs dedicated vector databases: when Postgres is enough](/blog/pgvector-vs-dedicated-vector-databases/): When Postgres with pgvector is enough, including its limits on dimensions, filtering and hybrid search, the signs you have outgrown it and how to test the choice on your own data.
- [Prompt engineering for production LLM apps](/blog/prompt-engineering-for-production-llm-apps/): How to structure, version and test prompts as application code: separating instructions from data, regression cases, staged rollout and rollback.
- [RAG for PDFs and tables: parsing awkward documents](/blog/rag-for-pdfs-and-tables/): How to prepare awkward documents for retrieval: sorting PDFs by type, recovering reading order, representing tables and checking extraction quality.
- [LangGraph tutorial for beginners: your first graph](/blog/langgraph-tutorial-for-beginners/): A step-by-step first graph that needs no API key: state, nodes, edges, conditional routing, a bounded loop and a checkpointer.
- [Document summarisation with LLMs](/blog/document-summarisation-with-llms/): Approaches for summarising long documents: whole-document prompts, map-reduce, refine, hierarchical and extract-first methods, plus how to check faithfulness.
- [How to scope an AI project before you build](/blog/how-to-scope-an-ai-project/): A buyer's guide to the decisions that come before an AI build: the problem, baseline, data, acceptable errors, human review, evaluation and ownership.
- [RAG chatbot vs custom GPT: when to build](/blog/rag-chatbot-vs-custom-gpt/): When a hosted assistant is enough, when building is justified, and a low-cost trial that settles the choice.
- [Multi-agent design patterns: supervisor, pipeline and handoff](/blog/multi-agent-design-patterns/): How each pattern works and fails, based on who picks the next step, plus how to pass context between agents.
- [FastAPI vs Flask for AI backends](/blog/fastapi-vs-flask-for-ai-backends/): Why FastAPI is the usual default for new LLM backends, and when Flask is still the right choice.
- [Sentiment analysis with Python: approaches and trade-offs](/blog/sentiment-analysis-with-python/): VADER, TF-IDF classifiers, pretrained transformers and LLMs compared, with a fair way to test them on your own data.
- [Testing AI agents: how to handle non-deterministic behaviour](/blog/testing-ai-agents/): Four test layers, from a scripted fake model to repeated scenarios judged by pass rate, with assertions on behaviour rather than wording.
- [AI agent security risks and the controls that address them](/blog/ai-agent-security-risks/): Risks of tool-using agents beyond prompt injection, including identity, secrets, network access, code execution, third-party tools and memory, with a control for each.
- [How to choose an LLM by testing it against your task](/blog/llm-model-selection-guide/): A seven-step way to choose a model through hard constraints, your own test set, fair scoring and keeping the model replaceable.
- [Building a React frontend for LLM chat apps](/blog/react-frontend-for-llm-chat-apps/): Message state, render performance, untrusted Markdown, scrolling, the composer, tool activity, errors and accessibility in a React chat UI.
- [SQL agents vs RAG: choosing by the shape of your data](/blog/sql-agents-vs-rag/): Choosing by question and data shape, handling awkward in-between data, and routing between the two.
- [When not to use AI agents, and what to build instead](/blog/when-not-to-use-ai-agents/): A ladder of simpler options, seven situations where simpler software wins, and a worked hypothetical built without an agent.
- [RAG access control: keeping retrieval within each user's permissions](/blog/rag-access-control-and-permissions/): How to enforce per-user permissions in the search itself, keep them in sync, close side channels and test for leaks.
- [LLM caching strategies: exact and semantic caching and their risks](/blog/llm-caching-strategies/): Cache key design, treating a semantic cache as a classifier to be evaluated, and the risks of leaks, staleness and poisoning.
- [How to build an AI document processing pipeline](/blog/ai-document-processing-pipeline/): The stages from intake to audit, with validation in code, review design, measurement and gradual automation.
- [Conversational AI vs chatbots: what differs and how to choose](/blog/conversational-ai-vs-chatbots/): Compares scripted, intent-based and LLM designs, their failure modes, hybrids and six questions for choosing.
- [How to hire an AI engineer: what to look for and what to ask](/blog/hire-an-ai-engineer-what-to-look-for/): A buyer's guide covering the evidence that counts, 14 questions, warning signs and a small paid test.
